source_read: PMC full text PMC3280662 (Neuropsychopharmacology 2012;37(4):1072-1073), read in this reader's own browser tab (tab-7): all five running-text paragraphs, author information, article notes (received 16 August 2011, accepted 19 August 2011), acknowledgments, competing interests and the seven references. The publisher's page was not opened and no sign-in was attempted.

design.note: A reply letter with no data; narrative-review plus the design_detail is the workable label, and the detail that the criticized study and the critics' letter were not read is correctly stated.

key_findings.note: 1st paragraph: 'considerable agreement ... regarding the need for well-controlled longitudinal studies', with the claim that the concerns were addressed in the original report.
2nd paragraph, including the explicit disclaimers about a common cause and about dementia rates.

3rd paragraph: the critics' combined correlation, the below-mean/above-mean pattern, the 3 to 155 episode range, and the claim that including controls obscures a 'strong dose-response relationship' evident with ranked data. No figures are given, as the card says.
4th paragraph, including the prospective impulsivity citation (printed in the text as 'de Winn et al, 2007').

reporting_issues.note: Neither the original correlations nor the reanalysis appears with a coefficient, an interval or an n anywhere in the letter.
'de Winn et al, 2007' in the 4th paragraph against 'de Win MM' in the reference list.

domains.note: Five of seven references are the author's group's; I counted Bauernfeind, Cowan 2006, Cowan 2008, Karageorgiou and Salomon, which matches.
some-concerns is defensible because the causal sentence is marked as a belief; the sentence it rests on about primate neurotoxicity is itself uncited (see missed).

interpretation_gap.note: Substantial. A pattern that runs below the control mean at low exposure and above it at high exposure is described in passing and then called a strong dose-response relationship, with no test offered and no numbers reported.

missed: The sentence that 'MDMA has a well-established ability to cause serotonin neurotoxicity in non-human primates' carries no citation of its own; the paragraph's citations are to the author's group's human studies. cl_mdma_sert_binding anchors on this paragraph, so the absence of a source should be on the card.

The claimed dose-response relationship is said to be evident 'when ranked data is used to properly account for the non-parametric distribution of lifetime MDMA use'. The card mentions ranked data in the interpretation gap; it belongs in the key findings too, since the relationship exists only after that transformation and is never given as a coefficient.

The letter gives no group sizes, no abstinence interval and no exposure distribution beyond the 3 to 155 range, so nothing in it can be checked or re-analysed. The card says this for the reanalysis; it is true of the defended study as described here as well.
